metadata.title: How classroom management and instructional clarity relate to students' academic emotions in Hong Kong and England: A multi-group analysis based on the control-value theory

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TIMSS 2019 grade 8 mathematics data from Hong Kong and England, selecting students with native-born parents and restricting analyses to mathematics classrooms. The authors address missing item responses using full-information maximum likelihood (FIML) in Mplus and estimate a latent multi-group structural equation model with the Mplus TYPE = COMPLEX option to account for the nested data structure and compute robust standard errors. The manuscript does not report the use of explicit student/sampling weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight procedures, so it is unclear whether complex survey weights were applied beyond the TYPE = COMPLEX robust SE adjustment. No outlier trimming or additional grade/school filtering beyond the native-parent criterion is described.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used TIMSS 2019 grade 8 mathematics classroom data for Hong Kong and England. Restricted the analytic sample to students with native-born parents to ensure sample purity. Final analysis included 1146 students from 142 classes in Hong Kong and 1981 students from 158 classes in England. Missing data on observed items (0.4%–2.9% per item) was handled via FIML in Mplus rather than listwise deletion.

main_findings.dataset_used: TIMSS 2019 Grade 8 Mathematics (Hong Kong vs England) — mathematics achievement (Plausible Values)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Latent multi-group SEM fit: χ2(792)=4004.398, RMSEA=0.051, SRMR=0.070, TLI=0.924, CFI=0.930. Explained variance: 17.9% (Hong Kong) and 32.4% (England). Key standardized paths: Hong Kong self-concept→achievement β=0.153 (p=.006); value→achievement β=0.158 (p<.001). England management→achievement β=0.205 (p<.001); clarity→achievement β=-0.108 (p<.001); self-concept→achievement β=0.413 (p<.001); value→achievement β=-0.033 (p=.176).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2019 Grade 8 Mathematics the study leveraged home resources (books), gender, age, mathematics self-concept, and mathematics value to model mathematics achievement (PVs) in a two-group (Hong Kong vs England) latent multi-group SEM, finding that self-concept and value were positively associated with achievement in Hong Kong, while in England classroom management and instructional clarity showed direct effects (management positive; clarity negative) and achievement was strongly related to self-concept but not value. This indicates that strengthening students’ mathematics self-concept may be a broadly effective route to higher achievement, whereas the role of instructional clarity may differ by educational context and could even backfire on achievement in some settings.

main_findings.dataset_used: TIMSS 2019 Grade 8 Mathematics (Hong Kong vs England) — enjoyment (Likert-scale latent factor)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Explained variance: 63.7% (Hong Kong) and 59.9% (England). Key standardized paths (Hong Kong): management→enjoyment β=0.066 (p=.005); clarity→enjoyment β=0.164 (p<.001); self-concept→enjoyment β=0.646 (p<.001); value→enjoyment β=0.182 (p<.001). Key standardized paths (England): management→enjoyment β=0.005 (p=.837); clarity→enjoyment β=0.148 (p<.001); self-concept→enjoyment β=0.655 (p<.001); value→enjoyment β=0.190 (p<.001). Indirect effects: management→self-concept→enjoyment β=-0.118 (p<.001) in Hong Kong and β=0.077 (p=.011) in England; clarity→self-concept→enjoyment β=0.294 (p<.001) in Hong Kong and β=0.229 (p<.001) in England.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2019 Grade 8 Mathematics the study leveraged home resources (books), gender, age, classroom management, instructional clarity, mathematics self-concept, and mathematics value to model mathematics enjoyment, finding that instructional clarity had positive direct effects on enjoyment in both Hong Kong and England, while classroom management showed a positive direct effect in Hong Kong but not in England. The mediation results further showed that enjoyment was consistently linked to self-concept and value across both contexts. This indicates that improving clarity of mathematics instruction may reliably enhance students’ positive learning emotions, while the emotional payoff of classroom management depends on the educational system.

main_findings.dataset_used: TIMSS 2019 Grade 8 Mathematics (Hong Kong vs England) — boredom (Likert-scale latent factor)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Explained variance: 21.7% (Hong Kong) and 43.3% (England). Key standardized paths (Hong Kong): management→boredom β=-0.191 (p<.001); clarity→boredom β=-0.029 (p=.531, n.s.); self-concept→boredom β=-0.389 (p<.001); value→boredom β=-0.127 (p=.006). Key standardized paths (England): management→boredom β=-0.125 (p<.001); clarity→boredom β=-0.077 (p=.022); self-concept→boredom β=-0.498 (p<.001); value→boredom β=-0.251 (p<.001). Indirect effects: management→self-concept→boredom β=0.071 (p<.001) in Hong Kong and β=-0.038 (p=.011) in England; clarity→self-concept→boredom β=-0.177 (p<.001) in Hong Kong and β=-0.174 (p<.001) in England.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2019 Grade 8 Mathematics the study leveraged home resources (books), gender, age, classroom management, instructional clarity, mathematics self-concept, and mathematics value to model mathematics boredom, finding that classroom management was negatively associated with boredom in both Hong Kong and England, while instructional clarity reduced boredom only in England (not directly in Hong Kong). Across both contexts, boredom was strongly and negatively related to mathematics self-concept and also negatively related to mathematics value. This indicates that classroom management strategies that reduce disruptive behavior may lower negative emotions broadly, but instructional clarity may need context-sensitive implementation to consistently reduce boredom.

data.outcome_summary: This study analyzed TIMSS 2019 grade 8 mathematics data from Hong Kong and England, focusing on two teaching characteristics (classroom management and instructional clarity) and their links to two academic emotions (enjoyment and boredom) via cognitive appraisals (mathematics self-concept and value). The analytic sample was restricted to students with native-born parents (Hong Kong: 1146; England: 1981) and missing item responses (0.4%–2.9% per item) were handled with FIML in Mplus. The authors used a latent multi-group SEM with TYPE = COMPLEX and integrated results across five plausible values for mathematics achievement. Model fit was acceptable (e.g., χ2(792)=4004.398, RMSEA=0.051, CFI=0.930), and the model explained substantial variance in enjoyment (63.7% HK; 59.9% England) and boredom (21.7% HK; 43.3% England). Key limitations are that the study is not an ML predictive modeling paper (no ML algorithms or ML metrics like AUC/RMSE are reported) and that causal claims are not warranted from cross-sectional SEM paths.
